identity_marker: yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes
continuity_anchors: on a brightly lit laboratory table with a neutral grey background
video_goal: Demonstrate how to measure the voltage of a zinc-copper sulfate galvanic cell using a Fluke 101 multimeter.
single_prompt: From an over-the-shoulder view, a glass beaker filled with bright blue copper sulfate solution, a silvery zinc strip, and a reddish-brown copper strip sits ready for the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The silvery zinc strip and reddish-brown copper strip rest partially submerged inside the bright blue liquid, awaiting measurement by the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The entire setup remains on a brightly lit laboratory table with a neutral grey background, highlighting the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The camera smoothly transitions to a top-down view, revealing the glass beaker and the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. A hand enters the frame and places the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes directly on the table next to the beaker. This action unfolds on a brightly lit laboratory table with a neutral grey background, clearly displaying the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The camera glides into a close-up angle focusing directly on the central dial of the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. A thumb presses against the dial of the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes, rotating it from the 'OFF' position to the 'V' DC Voltage setting. The device sits securely on a brightly lit laboratory table with a neutral grey background, illuminating the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. Shifting smoothly to a first-person view, the camera looks down at the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. Two hands reach down and pick up the cables attached to the bottom ports of the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The hands and equipment are positioned on a brightly lit laboratory table with a neutral grey background, framing the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The camera moves into a tight close-up on the beaker and the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The left hand presses the sharp metal tip of the black probe from the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes firmly against the dry, exposed top of the silvery zinc strip. The reaction vessel rests on a brightly lit laboratory table with a neutral grey background, alongside the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. Maintaining the close-up angle, the camera pans slightly to follow the components of the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The right hand presses the metal tip of the red probe from the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes against the dry, exposed top of the reddish-brown copper strip. The metals and solution sit on a brightly lit laboratory table with a neutral grey background, connected to the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The camera pushes in for a macro shot of the contact points created by the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. Both probe tips of the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes are held steady against the respective metal strips, with the blue copper sulfate solution visible just below. The microscopic details are captured on a brightly lit laboratory table with a neutral grey background, emphasizing the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The hands lift and swap the positions of the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes, now pressing the red probe against the zinc strip and the black probe against the copper strip. This swap occurs on a brightly lit laboratory table with a neutral grey background, featuring the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The camera glides into a close-up once again, targeting the display of the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The clear digital readout shines on a brightly lit laboratory table with a neutral grey background, displaying the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. Shifting to an over-the-shoulder view, the camera captures the user finishing the measurement with the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. The resting equipment lies on a brightly lit laboratory table with a neutral grey background, alongside the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes. A thumb rotates the central dial of the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes back to the 'OFF' position, causing the digital screen to go blank. The powered-down device remains on a brightly lit laboratory table with a neutral grey background, concluding the demonstration of the yellow and grey Fluke 101 digital multimeter with red and black test probes.
